problem.summary: 从受噪声污染的测量值 y = Af + e 中精确恢复原始输入向量 f ∈ R^n，其中 A 是编码矩阵，e 是任意未知的错误向量。

motivation.summary: 解决编码理论中的经典纠错问题，以及欠定线性方程组的稀疏解问题。传统方法在错误比例较大时失效，需要一种在更广泛条件下有效的恢复方法。

core_idea.summary: 通过求解 ℓ1 最小化问题 min_{g∈R^n} ∥y - Ag∥_{ℓ1} 来精确恢复 f，该问题可转化为线性规划。其成功的关键在于编码矩阵 A 满足“一致不确定性原理”（Uniform Uncertainty Principle）。

method.summary: 1. 将解码问题转化为欠定系统 F d = ˜y 的稀疏解问题，其中 F 是 A 的零空间矩阵。2. 使用 ℓ1 最小化（基追踪）代替 NP 难的 ℓ0 最小化来寻找稀疏解。3. 证明在矩阵 F 满足受限等距性质（RIP）或类似条件时，ℓ1 最小化能精确恢复稀疏向量。4. 对于随机高斯矩阵，证明其以极高概率满足所需条件。

experiments.summary: 数值实验表明，即使在输出被显著比例（如 m=2n 时低于 17%，m=4n 时低于 34%）的条目损坏的情况下，ℓ1 恢复程序仍能精确恢复输入向量 f。

claims.claim: 在编码矩阵 A 满足适当条件（如 F 满足 δ_{2S} < √2 - 1）且错误向量 e 的支撑大小 ∥e∥_{ℓ0} ≤ ρ·m 时，f 是 ℓ1 最小化问题 (P'_1) 的唯一解。
ℓ1 最小化问题可以重述为线性规划问题。
对于随机高斯矩阵，当错误比例 r = S/m 足够小时（例如 p/m=3/4 时 r ≤ 3.6×10^{-4}），恢复条件以极高概率成立。
数值实验验证了 ℓ1 恢复在错误比例高达约 17% (m=2n) 和 34% (m=4n) 时仍然有效。
ℓ1 最小化成功的关键在于矩阵满足“一致不确定性原理”（Uniform Uncertainty Principle）或 RIP。

limitations.limitation: 理论保证中的错误比例上界 ρ 非常小（例如 10^{-4} 量级），远低于实验观察到的有效比例，表明理论界限是悲观的。
构造满足所需条件的确定性矩阵可能很困难。
方法假设错误是稀疏的（ℓ0 范数有界），对于非稀疏错误模型可能不适用。

nodes.title: 问题建模
nodes.label: Problem Formulation
nodes.summary: 将解码问题形式化为从 y = Af + e 中恢复 f，其中 A 是 m×n 编码矩阵，e 是未知错误向量。
nodes.description: 考虑输入向量 f ∈ R^n，通过编码矩阵 A 生成码字 Af ∈ R^m。接收到的测量值 y 是码字与任意错误向量 e 的和。目标是从 y 中精确恢复 f。

nodes.title: 转化为稀疏恢复问题
nodes.label: Reduction to Sparse Recovery
nodes.summary: 通过构造零空间矩阵 F (FA=0)，将解码问题转化为从 ˜y = Fe 中恢复稀疏向量 e 的问题。
nodes.description: 定义 F 为满足 FA=0 的矩阵。将 y 左乘 F 得到 ˜y = F(Af+e) = Fe。因此，恢复 f 的问题等价于从欠定系统 Fd = ˜y 中找到稀疏解 d=e。

nodes.title: ℓ1 最小化解码
nodes.label: ℓ1 Minimization Decoding
nodes.summary: 提出使用 ℓ1 最小化 min_{g∈R^n} ∥y - Ag∥_{ℓ1} 来恢复 f，该问题可转化为线性规划。
nodes.description: 直接求解 ℓ1 最小化问题 (P'_1): min_{g∈R^n} ∥y - Ag∥_{ℓ1}。证明该问题与求解 (P1): min ∥d∥_{ℓ1} s.t. Fd = ˜y 等价。ℓ1 最小化问题可以重述为线性规划 (LP)，从而高效求解。

nodes.title: 受限等距性质 (RIP)
nodes.label: Restricted Isometry Property (RIP)
nodes.summary: 定义矩阵 F 的受限等距常数 δ_S，用于量化其子矩阵的近似正交性，这是 ℓ1 恢复成功的理论基础。
nodes.description: 对于矩阵 F，定义其 S-受限等距常数 δ_S 为满足 (1-δ_S)∥c∥_2^2 ≤ ∥F_T c∥_2^2 ≤ (1+δ_S)∥c∥_2^2 对所有 |T|≤S 成立的最小常数。类似定义受限正交常数 θ_{S,S'}。这些常数衡量了 F 的列向量集合在稀疏子集上的近似正交性。

nodes.title: 主要恢复定理
nodes.label: Main Recovery Theorem
nodes.summary: 证明如果矩阵 F 满足 δ_{2S} < √2 - 1，则任何 S-稀疏向量 c 都是 ℓ1 最小化问题 (P1) 的唯一解。
nodes.description: 定理 1.4 和 1.5 表明，如果 F 的受限等距常数 δ_{2S} < √2 - 1，那么对于任何支撑大小 ≤ S 的向量 c，其 ℓ1 最小化解是唯一的。这直接保证了从 y = Af + e 中恢复 f 的唯一性，其中 e 的支撑大小 ≤ S。

nodes.title: 随机矩阵的 RIP 保证
nodes.label: RIP Guarantee for Random Matrices
nodes.summary: 证明随机高斯矩阵以极高概率满足 RIP 条件，从而为 ℓ1 恢复提供了概率性保证。
nodes.description: 定理 1.6 表明，对于 p×m 的随机高斯矩阵 F，当稀疏度比例 r = S/m 小于某个阈值 r*(p,m) 时，δ_{2S} < √2 - 1 以极高概率（概率随 m 指数衰减）成立。数值评估显示，例如当 p/m = 3/4 时，r ≤ 3.6×10^{-4}。

nodes.title: 数值实验验证
nodes.label: Numerical Experiments
nodes.summary: 通过数值实验验证 ℓ1 恢复在错误比例远高于理论界限时仍然有效。
nodes.description: 实验设置：A 为 m×n 随机高斯矩阵，f 为随机输入，e 为随机稀疏错误。结果表明，当 m=2n 时，错误比例低于约 17% 可精确恢复；当 m=4n 时，错误比例低于约 34% 可精确恢复。这远高于理论预测的极小阈值。

metadata.title: Decoding by linear programming
metadata.abstract: This paper considers a natural error correcting problem with real valued input/output. We wish to recover an input vector f/spl isin/R/sup n/ from corrupted measurements y=Af+e. Here, A is an m by n (coding) matrix and e is an arbitrary and unknown vector of errors. Is it possible to recover f exactly from the data y? We prove that under suitable conditions on the coding matrix A, the input f is the unique solution to the /spl lscr//sub 1/-minimization problem (/spl par/x/spl par//sub /spl lscr/1/:=/spl Sigma//sub i/|x/sub i/|) min(g/spl isin/R/sup n/) /spl par/y - Ag/spl par//sub /spl lscr/1/ provided that the support of the vector of errors is not too large, /spl par/e/spl par//sub /spl lscr/0/:=|{i:e/sub i/ /spl ne/ 0}|/spl les//spl rho//spl middot/m for some /spl rho/>0. In short, f can be recovered exactly by solving a simple convex optimization problem (which one can recast as a linear program). In addition, numerical experiments suggest that this recovery procedure works unreasonably well; f is recovered exactly even in situations where a significant fraction of the output is corrupted. This work is related to the problem of finding sparse solutions to vastly underdetermined systems of linear equations. 1 Introduction
1.1 Decoding of linear codes
This paper considers the model problem of recovering an inpu t vector f ∈ Rn from cor-
rupted measurements y = Af + e. Here, A is an m by n matrix (we will assume throughout

the paper that m > n ), and e is an arbitrary and unknown vector of errors. The problem we consider is whether it is possible to recover f exactly from the data y. And if so, how? In its abstract form, our problem is of course equivalent to t he classical error correcting problem which arises in coding theory as we may think of A as a linear code; a linear code is a given collection of codewords which are vectors a1, . . . , a n ∈ Rm—the columns of the matrix A. Given a vector f ∈ Rn (the “plaintext”) we can then generate a vector Af in Rm (the “ciphertext”); if A has full rank, then one can clearly recover the plaintext f from the ciphertext Af . But now we suppose that the ciphertext Af is corrupted by an arbitrary vector e ∈ Rm giving rise to the corrupted ciphertext Af + e. The question is then: given the coding matrix A and Af + e, can one recover f exactly?
As is well-known, if the fraction of the corrupted entries is too large, then of course we have
no hope of reconstructing f from Af + e; for instance, assume that m = 2 n and consider
two distinct plaintexts f, f ′ and form a vector g ∈ Rm by setting half of its m coeﬃcients

6 Discussion
6.1 Connections with other works
In our linear programming model, the plaintext and cipherte xt had real-valued components.
Another intensively studied model occurs when the plaintex t and ciphertext take values
in the ﬁnite ﬁeld F2 := {0, 1}. In recent work of Feldman et al. [17], [18], [19], linear
programming methods (based on relaxing the space of codewor ds to a convex polytope)

were developed to establish a polynomial-time decoder whic h can correct a constant fraction of errors, and also achieve the information-theoretic capa city of the code. There is thus some intriguing parallels between those works and the resul ts in this paper, however there appears to be no direct overlap as our methods are restricted to real-valued texts, and the
work cited above requires texts in F2. Also, our error analysis is deterministic and is thus

guaranteed to correct arbitrary errors provided that they a re suﬃciently sparse. The ideas presented in this paper may be adapted to recover in put vectors taking values from a ﬁnite alphabet. We hope to report on work in progress in a follow-up paper.

This paper introduced general results stating that it is pos sible to correct for errors by
ℓ 1-minimization. We then explained how the results specializ e in the case where the coding
